praevĭus , a, um, adj. prae-via,
I.going before, leading the way (poet.): praevius Aurorae, Solis Noctisque satelles, Cic. Arat. ap. Non. 65, 9: nunc praevius anteit, Ov. M. 11, 65: “praevia luci Pallantias,” id. ib. 15, 190 ; Stat. Th. 4, 485: “cui (luci) praevius est sol,” Aus. Idyll. Monosyllab. 12 ; Lact. 4, 24, 8; Amm. 14, 11, 18.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
